title: brain: theOS's memory, one schema, one door
note: brain is theOS's memory: one JSON doc per thing, a schema per type, the reflection (what a new doc supersedes) and the trace (which AIP step and author wrote it). Revision 5 adds the one door every read and write goes through: the brain command, its skill and an MCP server, with fixed verbs (D-41, D-46, D-47), learned from the research (aip/AIP-3/research).

questions.q: Is brain's direction right: a JSON doc per thing, JSON Lines for whatever only grows, a JSON Schema per type, binaries named by content hash, and every internal reference pinned as path@full commit SHA?
options: Yes, take it into AIP-3's Understand
Change it: tell me what

questions.q: brain, two simplifications the review proposes against your direction (D-12, D-25): keep each list that only grows as a JSON array with a prefix check instead of JSON Lines, and compute a link's version from git (the commit that added the citing line) instead of storing path@SHA?
options: Both (recommended: no history was rewritten yet, and the static apps cannot read git objects)
Keep JSON Lines and stored pins, as decided

Only the computed version

Keep c5 in checkpoint 4

MCP from the start

questions.q: Is withdraw (a doc stops holding with no successor, with its reason kept) a verb you want, or must every doc that stops holding be superseded by a newer one?
options: Withdraw, with its reason, only from an AIP's event (recommended)
Only supersede

questions.q: Hash ids (D-45): do D-1 to D-48, AIP-1 to AIP-6 and the other numbered docs keep their names as labels, or are they renamed?
options: Renamed once, every link rewritten in the same commit (recommended: one name per doc, nothing to keep in step)
Kept as labels beside the hash id

questions.q: How strict is brain add about the reflection: refuse a doc whose author skipped a candidate brain reflect listed, or let the reviewer judge?
options: The reviewer judges; brain refuses only a supersede of a doc that did not hold (recommended: whether a doc replaces another needs judgement)
brain add refuses
questions.answer: The reviewer judges: "reviewer to judge" (Samuel, in the AIP-3 thread, 2026-11-01)

questions.q: Hash ids for the docs that exist now: you said "you can rename them" (D-49). A review points out a third way: old docs keep their D-n and AIP-n ids, and only new docs get hash ids. Old ids were made one at a time and never collide, so this needs no migration, no exception to history only growing, and no rename map, and prose like "(D-41)" keeps working. Which?
options: Keep the old ids; only new docs get hash ids (recommended)
Rename every doc once (D-49 as written)

questions.q: Where do theOS sessions start? The brain prime hook and theOS/CLAUDE.md load only if a session's working folder is theOS/ (the repository root's .claude is legacy and not changed).
options: theOS threads start in theOS/ (recommended)
At the repository root, with the hook added to the root .claude by an exception

problem.experience: Decisions, words and history were kept in chat and in files edited in place: a newer decision did not say what it replaced, outdated words came back, and nobody could tell which step wrote what.

items.text: Decisions were listed oldest first, and a newer one did not say which older one it replaced (the dated decision docs, before D-15).
avenCEO had to be renamed by hand across 13 types, 25 terms and three apps, twice (D-17, D-21).
A read flag on 58 sources claimed a global truth that was per intent (D-22).
A link is a bare path, and the file behind it changes (D-12).

problem.baseline: Now: one JSON doc per thing in theOS/ (the counts are read off when Gate A is asked); the reflection and the trace computed by the apps; no schema, no check that history only grows, links by bare path.
whys: You can't be sure the agents follow what holds now. Why? Old and new decisions sat side by side, edited in place, without saying which replaces which.
Why? Memory had no rules: no schema per type, no history that only grows, no reflection, links that move.
Root cause: brain has no schema, and nothing enforces the reflection, the trace or the growth of history.
truths: Git keeps every version of every file; a commit SHA names exactly one.
What is computed from a log that only grows cannot drift from it.
A JSON Schema is checked by a program, without judgement.
Whether a new decision replaces an old one needs judgement: an agent proposes it, the decision records it.
A program that is the only way to write can refuse a bad write before it lands; a check after the fact can only fail the commit.
assumptions: One JSON doc per thing stays fast enough for the apps and the command at a few hundred docs.
Agents use the door when it is the only way that passes the check: an event can be typed by hand, so the check proves an event exists, not that the command wrote it.
problem.risk: Can be undone: every change is files in git.

reuse.what: theOS/ui/wiki.js: the crawl, the backlinks, W.trace and W.stepAt
reuse.use: Used: links, backlinks, the trace and the step (the functions trace and stepAt) are computed there already; brain loads the same file.

Learned from: a frozen verb protocol with a conformance test; one CLI as the only door and hash ids; edits that quote the version read; supersede, never delete.
Learned from, not touched: a log that only grows is checked by comparing it with its earlier version.

options.name: One door over the JSON docs in git: a command with fixed verbs and its skill, MCP for AIP-4; the check behind it
options.note: The direction you approved (D-25, D-31, D-32) with the door (D-41, D-46, D-47). The verbs come from gbrain's frozen protocol, Beads' only-door CLI, Basic Memory's guarded edits and Graphiti's never-delete supersession (aip/AIP-3/research).

options.name: Free writes to files, with only the check after
options.note: Rejected (D-41, D-46): an agent learns of a bad write only when the commit fails, and nothing teaches it the verbs.

options.name: A memory library: a model extracts facts, vector or graph search finds them (mem0, Zep, Cognee)
options.note: Rejected: brain records decisions explicitly; a model inside the door makes it non-deterministic. mem0 itself moved from model-chosen updates and deletes to add-only (sources/mem0).

options.name: A database
options.note: Rejected: git already versions, diffs and reviews files; a database would need its own history and review.

claims.promise: Every JSON doc in aip, decisions, sessions, sources, metrics, lessons, authors and avenCEO has a type with a type doc, and matches the JSON Schema inside it. by is always an author doc; every type a newer doc can supersede has about (its topics); a type doc lists the steps (1 to 4) at which its type may be written; a correction event names its cause (outdated-decision, outdated-word, missed-supersede or other).
claims.fails: A misspelt field, a missing or misspelt type, or a free-text author passes unseen.
claims.check: Validated with ajv; each schema rejects a planted bad doc of its type; every current doc passes.

claims.promise: brain protocol v1 is the one door: the command and the skill give every verb's documented answer and error codes; brain prime runs at session start and theOS/CLAUDE.md names it first.
claims.fails: Agents act on a superseded doc because they read raw files, or a verb answers differently than v1 says.
claims.check: A test runs every verb of v1 on the fixed docs in theOS/brain/test/ and compares with the expected answers; the hook file and CLAUDE.md's line name brain prime.

claims.promise: Every doc changed in a commit is covered by an event added in that commit, by an author doc, at a step (computed from the intent's events) where its type may be written (D-40, D-46).
claims.fails: A doc changes that no AIP step wrote.
claims.check: brain check (inside AIP-1's check command) fails a planted edit with no event, an event by a free string, and a write of a type at a step its type does not allow (a measurement outside Learn).

claims.promise: Every new doc gets a hash id minted by brain add (D-45), so parallel threads almost never pick the same one; when two do, the merge fails, and one is minted again.
claims.fails: Two threads create the same id and one silently overwrites the other.
claims.check: A test makes two branches add a decision each and merges them: no clash, the index written again by brain index, both events kept. A test with two branches adding the same id expects the merge to fail.

claims.promise: One reflection for every type: a new doc's supersedes entries ({doc, part, what}) each point at a doc that held at the parent commit; what holds is computed, never stored. The candidates the doc leaves unsuperseded are recorded in its event by brain add, and the reviewer judges them (D-50).
claims.fails: A doc supersedes something that no longer held, or points at nothing.
claims.check: brain add and brain check refuse a planted supersede of a doc already superseded at the parent, and one of a missing doc; a planted add records its left candidates in the event.

claims.promise: Links are brain's graph: every path inside a doc resolves, and each link's type is the field it sits in; brain get returns links and backlinks by type. brain check warns, without failing, when a doc that holds cites one that was superseded (D-48).
claims.fails: A link points at nothing, or a holding doc quietly rests on a superseded one.
claims.check: brain check fails a planted dangling path and prints a warning for a planted citation of a superseded doc.

claims.promise: If question 11 keeps the rename (D-49): the numbered docs are renamed once to hash ids in one migration commit, written by brain as one event of AIP-3 at Build; every path field (a string brain's link rule accepts) is rewritten, prose is not, and theOS/brain/renames.json maps each old name to its new id. It is the one named exception to c2.
claims.fails: A path still points at an old name, or an old name in prose can no longer be found.
claims.check: After the rename no path field holds an old name; brain get resolves every old name in renames.json.
claims.note: Waits on question 11; dropped if old ids are kept.

claims.promise: What only grows (an intent's events, a metric's measurements, a session's asks) stays a JSON array that only grows.
claims.fails: History is rewritten and nothing notices.
claims.check: brain check requires the parent's array to be a deep-equal prefix of the new one; a planted edit, deletion or reorder of an old entry fails.

claims.promise: No list is kept twice: session.decisions, session.intents and the definition's copied lists are deleted and computed by the apps from links; the index docs, which the static apps need, equal their folder because only brain index writes them.
claims.fails: A copy drifts, as session.intents did.
claims.check: brain check fails an index doc that differs from its folder, and a planted copied list in a session or the definition.

claims.promise: A term that renames a word carries the old word and where the rename applies, and the terms check fails when the old word comes back there, and stays quiet where its other meaning is right.
claims.fails: A rename sweep misses a place, or a word with two meanings raises a false alarm.
claims.check: A test plants each renamed word once where the rename applies and once where its other meaning is right.

claims.promise: The verbs of v1 are served over MCP from the same functions, for AIP-4's mod (D-47).
claims.fails: The mod reaches brain some other way.
claims.check: One smoke call per verb through the MCP server returns what the command returns.
claims.note: Waits on question 13: recommended to move into AIP-4.

outcome.promise: Over the three sessions after checkpoint 2: no correction whose cause is an outdated decision, an outdated word or a missed supersede.
outcome.how: Each correction event names its cause (c1). At Learn the measurement counts them per session from those events; the baseline is counted the same way at Gate A from this session's events.

checkpoints.adds: The door, smallest end to end, on AIP-1's check command, package.json and theOS/CLAUDE.md (AIP-1's checkpoint 1): every supersedes entry moved to {doc, part, what}; about added to the types that can be superseded; holds() moved from avenCEO/app.js into ui/wiki.js; schemas in the type docs, with each type's steps as data (avenMAIA writes the type docs); brain prime, holds, get, add (hash ids for new docs), edit, append and index, its skill, the hook in theOS/.claude/settings.json and one line in theOS/CLAUDE.md; brain check failing a doc changed without an event.
The reflection (brain reflect; supersedes checked at the parent; left candidates recorded); the link graph by type and its audit; the rename if question 11 keeps it; then lists that only grow.
Copied lists deleted and computed (avenMAIA's docs); renames as term docs and the terms check.
The MCP server over the same functions, if question 13 keeps it in AIP-3, after AIP-4 passes Gate A.

deferred.what: The maintenance pass: a fresh agent turns brain check's warnings and missed supersedes into proposed writes through the same verbs, in an AIP's step
deferred.until: Three sessions without a correction whose cause is a missed supersede, or warnings pile up faster than they are fixed.

deferred.what: brain changes --since <commit>: what changed since a point, for a thread coming back
deferred.until: A thread rereads brain often enough to need it.

deferred.what: A 'valid from' date apart from the commit time
deferred.until: A decision is recorded after it took effect.

deferred.what: brain edit --expect <sha>: refuse an edit of a doc changed since it was read
deferred.until: Two writers share one working tree.

deferred.what: A link's version computed from git, flagged when its target changed since it was cited (was c5: A link's version is computed, never stored: the version cited is the commit that added the citing line, and the check flags a link whose target changed since.)
deferred.until: Question 3 keeps it, or a correction is traced to a link whose target moved.

source.text: Let's settle the schema of our single source of truth for everything we generate in AIPs, learnings and sources: what is a JSON file, what is a list of JSON entries, what is markdown, and what is both. And link every internal git resource by its commit hash, never by a bare file path, because history changes.

protocol.name: brain protocol v1
protocol.what: The one door to brain (D-41). One program, theOS/brain/brain.mjs, with these verbs. The command line and the skill (theOS/brain/SKILL.json, which teaches only these verbs) call it now; an MCP server calls the same functions for AIP-4's mod (a Claude Code plugin, AIP-4's work, that shows theOS's intents and brain inside Claude Code) once AIP-4 passes Gate A (D-47). Fields keep their meaning forever; v1 only grows (new verbs, new optional fields). brain writes files; the agent commits them with its other work.

reads.does: Prints the decisions and terms that hold now (id and title) and what waits for Samuel (open questions and his tasks); brain holds <type> gives the rest. A Claude Code hook runs it at the start of a session and after compaction (when Claude Code shortens a long conversation to fit). The hook lives in theOS/.claude/settings.json and theOS/CLAUDE.md names brain prime first; both load when a session's working folder is theOS/ (question 12).

Lists the docs of a type that hold now, from the one holds() in ui/wiki.js that the apps also use: a doc holds unless a doc that holds supersedes it. The result does not depend on the order branches were merged.

Returns one doc, what supersedes it, and its links and backlinks (a link is any string that names a doc's path). From checkpoint 2 the links are grouped by type: the field they sit in, such as supersedes, relates, intents or writes.
Lists the docs of the same type that hold now and share a topic (about) with the draft: the candidates it may supersede. The author judges.

protocol.writes_rule: Every write takes --intent (an AIP) and --by (an author doc). brain computes the step from that intent's events (the same stepAt the apps use: an AIP stands at the first step whose output is missing) and refuses a write its type does not allow at that step. It writes the doc and appends the event to that intent; the agent commits both together, and brain check fails a commit where they are apart.

writes.does: Mints the doc's id: <folder>/<prefix>-<hex>, the prefix short for the type (d for a decision, aip for an intent) and the hex the first 4 characters of a hash of the content, the time and a random salt, longer if the path exists on this branch (D-45). avenMAIA mints a decision's id this way like anyone else. Checks the doc against its type's schema; refuses a supersedes entry ({doc, part, what}) whose doc does not exist or did not hold at the parent commit. Runs brain reflect itself and writes into the event the candidates the doc does not supersede, for the reviewer to judge (D-50). Runs brain index when the doc's folder has one. Answers created or unchanged, and lists what the doc supersedes.
Changes a doc in place for a correction that keeps its meaning (a typo, a title, D-37); a change of meaning is a new doc that supersedes it. Answers changed or unchanged.
Adds an entry to the end of a list that only grows (events, measurements, asks). Answers appended.

Writes every index doc from its folder (the static apps cannot list a folder). It runs inside the write that needs it, and the index is listed in that event's writes; it is never edited by hand, so a merge clash in one is resolved by running it again.

check.does: A module that AIP-1's check command runs on every commit before it is pushed, by the done rule (theOS has no CI). It runs every claim's check below and fails a commit that changed a doc without an event of that commit (D-46). A commit is checked against its parent; a merge commit against its first parent, where only index docs written again by brain index and list entries appended on either side may differ (both kept, the first parent's first).

protocol.errors: Every refusal is a fixed code with the fix, for example no_intent (pass --intent aip/<id>), schema (field x: expected y), step (a <type> is written in <step>; the AIP stands at <step>), not_held (<id> was superseded by <id>).
not: No delete and no withdraw: a doc stops holding only when a newer doc supersedes it through the reflection (D-48).
No model inside the door: brain never guesses a supersede or a link.
No commits by brain, and no version guard on edit yet: each thread writes its own branch, so clashes show at merge.
